title: R. Yehudah bar Titus
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A student of R. Acha, in whose name he reported [teachings], [as in] Berakhot ch. 3 halakhah 4, Sukkah ch. 8 halakhah 8; and in Shabbat ch. 13 halakhah 2, [there is] R. Y. bar Titus, R. Yehudah ben Pazi, Shimon bar Ba, in the name of R. Yochanan. And in Bikkurim ch. 3, end of halakhah 3, [it says] that he needed to go to Rome, and they ordained him temporarily on condition that he return to the Land of Israel, and R. Chama called him Yehudah bar Titas. Of those who speak in his name, we find that the Rabbanan of Caesarea said [a teaching] in his name, as in Gittin ch. 5 halakhah 10, Avodah Zarah ch. 2 halakhah 3. And in Knesset HaGedolah on Yoreh De’ah, he cites in the name of the book Tamim De'im that it should read R. Yehudah ben Antigonus, for how is it possible for an Israelite to be called by the name Titus? It seems more likely that it should read R. Y. bar Sitos, as in Shevi'it, end of ch. 5, and that the samekh was mistakenly turned into a tet.[^2][^3]

notes.text: The English heading follows the supplied proofread heading ר׳ יהודה בר טיטוס, while the catalog metadata has בר מימוס. Titus, Titas and Sitos are kept distinct wherever Hyman uses them. No catalog identity or heading record has been changed.

כנ״הג ביו״ד is read contextually as Knesset HaGedolah, Yoreh De’ah. The [National Library of Israel’s Benveniste catalog](https://www.nli.org.il/en/a-topic/987007300354705171) lists Knesset HaGedolah on Yoreh De’ah; this supports the work-title expansion, not independent verification of the cited passage. תמים דעים is transliterated Tamim De’im. The personal initial ר״י remains R. Y., without a guessed expansion.

Hyman prints Sukkah ch. 8, halakhah 8, although Sukkah has no eighth chapter. The citation is reproduced as printed and remains unresolved; Sotah or any other tractate is not silently substituted. The other locators likewise follow Hyman, including Shabbat פ״יג. His discussion of proposed name changes and ‘It seems more likely’ retains its original attribution and degree of certainty.
